info.title: Neat Insight API
info.description:
Neat Insight provides an HTTP control plane for importing media, discovering viewer URLs, and inspecting runtime health. The same API drives the Insight web application and can be used from scripts, test automation, or development tools.

## Before you begin

- The default local endpoint is `https://127.0.0.1:9900`. Development installations normally use a locally generated certificate, so diagnostic clients may need to trust mkcert or use `curl -k`.
- Call `GET /api/health` before a workflow to confirm that the backend is ready.
- Media paths are always relative to their managed root. Absolute paths and traversal outside that root are rejected.
- vf viewer channel indexes are **zero-based**.
- Operations that import media may return a streaming `text/plain` progress response. Read through the final line before deciding whether the operation succeeded.

## Typical workflows

1. **Import media:** validate a YouTube URL, then import a clip of it into the media library.
2. **Open a viewer:** request `/api/viewer-url` so the URL reflects the current host and configured SDK channel capacity.
3. **Troubleshoot delivery:** check ingest statistics first; if RTP reaches vf but the browser still fails, continue with egress statistics.

## Security

The API has no application-level authentication. Expose it only on trusted development networks and place an authenticated gateway in front of it if broader access is required.

tags.name: API documentation
tags.description: Open the embedded Swagger UI or download the authoritative OpenAPI 3.1 document for generators, validators, and external documentation systems.

tags.name: Service and system
tags.description: Confirm readiness. System Info, the board, Peripherals and Stats are served by Insight's server (server/api/openapi.yaml).

tags.name: Media imports
tags.description: Populate the media library with YouTube clips: validate a URL, then download and transcode a clip of it. The import streams human-readable progress.

tags.name: Viewer
tags.description: Generate the URL of the viewer page, reachable from the current browser and bounded to the configured channel capacity, and relay the viewer's WebRTC offers to vf. Viewer channel indexes are zero-based even though media-source slots are one-based.

get.description: Returns the Swagger UI bundled with Insight. Use it for quick exploration against the current installation; use `/api/openapi.json` when a tool needs the machine-readable contract.

Returns the exact OpenAPI 3.1 document used by the embedded Swagger UI and the generated core documentation. The document is suitable for linting, client generation, contract tests, and documentation builds.

200.description: OpenAPI 3.1 document for the current Insight API.

get.description: A lightweight readiness probe that also reports the startup-scoped browser network configuration applied to vf and MediaMTX. Call this first from automation; a `200` response confirms that the Flask backend can accept subsequent API requests. A present but invalid `browser-ice-address` configuration prevents Insight from starting. A full HTTP(S) `launch-url` is reduced to its origin; an invalid launch URL preserves legacy request-host/port-map URL generation.

post.description: Inspects a YouTube URL without downloading the media and returns the title, duration, thumbnail, and supported Insight transcode targets. Call this before starting an import so a UI or script can show the user the actual clip metadata and reject unsupported inputs early.

200.description: Video title, duration, thumbnail, and supported import targets.

post.summary: Import and transcode a YouTube clip
post.description: Downloads the selected clip segment and transcodes it to an Insight-compatible MP4 rendition. The response is a streaming progress log; imports can take significant time and clients should keep the connection open through the final status line. Clip duration is capped at five minutes to bound resource use.

ProgressStream.description: Streaming progress messages. Inspect the final lines to determine whether the operation completed or failed.

Error.description: Standard JSON error envelope returned by most failed API operations.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason suitable for logs and user-facing diagnostics.

Health.description: Readiness result for the Insight Flask backend.

status.description: Fixed readiness state returned when the backend can serve requests.

service.description: Stable service identifier for automated probes.

time.description: Backend UTC time when the response was created.

network.description: Startup-scoped browser networking values applied by this Insight process.

browser_ice_address.description: Address advertised to browsers by vf and MediaMTX, or null when no override is active. The opt-in browser-ice-address file accepts IPv4; a legacy CONTAINER_HOST_IP fallback can also be IPv6.

browser_ice_address_source.description: Configuration source used for the effective browser ICE address.

public_origin.description: Trusted browser-facing HTTP origin used for viewer, WHIP, and MJPEG URLs, or null for request-host and port-map behavior.

YoutubeUrlRequest.description: YouTube video URL to inspect or import.

url.description: Public YouTube watch or share URL supported by the backend downloader.

YoutubeImportRequest.description: Selects the output rendition and optional bounded clip range for a YouTube import.

target.description: Insight-compatible resolution and frame-rate rendition to generate.

clip_duration.description: Number of seconds to import, capped at five minutes.
